T: Put on a show. Put out the snacks.
D: Walter, Gary and Mary get the Muppets back together to save their old theatre from an oil baron.
P: Serve the snacks when the telethon finally goes live.
S: Round loaf stuffed with cheddar, mozzarella and garlic butter. Tear and share, wocka wocka.

A cob loaf cut deep in a crisscross, stuffed with cheddar, mozzarella and garlic chive butter, baked until bubbling for everyone manning the phones. Cut a cob loaf in a crisscross pattern about 3cm apart, going deep but not through the base. Melt 100g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves and a handful of chopped chives. Push 150g grated cheddar and 150g grated mozzarella into the cuts and spoon the garlic butter over. Wrap in foil and bake at 180C for 15 minutes, then open the foil and bake 10 minutes more until the cheese bubbles. Put it in the middle of the table and pull apart.
Pork and beef meatballs simmered in cream gravy, lingonberry jam on the side. Bork, bork, bork.
Pork and beef meatballs with onion and allspice, browned and simmered in a creamy gravy, served with lingonberry jam on toothpicks.
Buttered popcorn in paper bags. Statler and Waldorf hated it, then finished the bag.

Heat the oil in a large lidded pot with three kernels. When they pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover and shake over the heat until the popping slows. Tip into a bowl, pour over the melted butter, toss with the salt and fill paper bags.
M: Ham and gruyère grilled sandwich under bubbling cheese sauce. Moi insists on a knife and fork.

Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk and cook until thick. Stir in half the gruyère, the mustard and nutmeg. Make four sandwiches of bread, ham and a little sauce, then spread the rest of the sauce on top, scatter with the rest of the gruyère and grill at 220°C until bubbling and browned. Serve with a green salad.
Sticky honey and soy chicken drumsticks, eaten with your hands. Drum solo optional.

Mix the honey, soy sauce, garlic and sesame oil and coat the drumsticks. Roast on a lined tray at 200°C for 40 minutes, turning and basting twice, until sticky and dark. Scatter with sesame seeds and spring onion and serve with plenty of napkins.
W: Cookie base, green peppermint icing and dark chocolate on top. It's not easy being green.
Biscuit base topped with a pale green peppermint icing and a dark chocolate top, chilled and cut into squares.
K: Cranberry, pineapple and orange juice layered into a rainbow, lemon-lime soda on top.
Orange, pineapple and cranberry juice layered over ice and topped with lemonade.

s.note: Pork and beef meatballs simmered in cream gravy, lingonberry jam on the side. Bork, bork, bork.
s.how: Mix 250g pork mince and 250g beef mince with a grated onion and a pinch of allspice. Roll into small balls and brown. Add 200ml cream and a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes. Serve on toothpicks with lingonberry jam. Bork bork.

s.note: Buttered popcorn in paper bags. Statler and Waldorf hated it, then finished the bag.
s.how: Heat the oil in a large lidded pot with three kernels. When they pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover and shake over the heat until the popping slows. Tip into a bowl, pour over the melted butter, toss with the salt and fill paper bags.

m.note: Sticky honey and soy chicken drumsticks, eaten with your hands. Drum solo optional.
m.how: Mix the honey, soy sauce, garlic and sesame oil and coat the drumsticks. Roast on a lined tray at 200°C for 40 minutes, turning and basting twice, until sticky and dark. Scatter with sesame seeds and spring onion and serve with plenty of napkins.

m.note: Ham and gruyère grilled sandwich under bubbling cheese sauce. Moi insists on a knife and fork.
m.how: Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk and cook until thick. Stir in half the gruyère, the mustard and nutmeg. Make four sandwiches of bread, ham and a little sauce, then spread the rest of the sauce on top, scatter with the rest of the gruyère and grill at 220°C until bubbling and browned. Serve with a green salad.

w.note: Cookie base, green peppermint icing and dark chocolate on top. It's not easy being green.
w.how: Crush 250g sweet biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 300g icing sugar with a little butter, peppermint essence and green colouring and spread over. Pour melted dark chocolate on top, chill and cut into squares.

d.note: Cranberry, pineapple and orange juice layered into a rainbow, lemon-lime soda on top.
d.how: Fill tall glasses with ice. Pour in cranberry juice first, then slowly add pineapple juice and orange juice over the back of a spoon so they layer. Top with lemonade. A rainbow in a glass for the show.
